Resource: Stripe, APIs as infrastructure (versioning) (~15 min), rolling versions with compatibility transforms, gold standard
facts.where: Further reading; Reading s-ver (quotes, versions animation)

facts.where: Further reading; Reading s-rest, s-err, s-page, s-ver cite rules #106, #108, #112, #115, #129, #134, #160, #176, #230

facts.where: owned by code_design; Further reading notes the move

facts.where: owned by code_design; Further reading notes the move

facts.old: Resource: Pydantic documentation (~1h30), the contract layer for modern Python services and libraries
Versioning: version the contract, not the URL aesthetics
Stripe model: each breaking change a dated version; server stores transforms between adjacent versions; pins each consumer to the version they onboarded with; core speaks only latest
facts.where: Reading s-ver (quotes and the dated-versions walk)
facts.verdict: verified, made precise: pinned on the account's first request; Stripe-Version header overrides per request; close to 100 incompatible upgrades over six years

facts.old: Cheaper variant: major version in the path (/v1/) plus additive-only changes within it
facts.verdict: kept; OpenAI and Anthropic use /v1/; Zalando forbids URL versioning (#115), added as the counterview

facts.old: Breaking = removing/renaming a field, tightening validation, changing semantics; adding optional fields is not breaking
facts.where: Reading s-ver lists; Breaking or not? tab
facts.verdict: verified against AIP-180 and Anthropic's versioning policy; added: changing defaults is breaking (AIP-180)

facts.old: Clients must ignore unknown fields (tolerant reader)
LLM APIs: the model is part of the contract surface; pin model versions; announce deprecations with dates
facts.verdict: kept; linked to Production eval engineering; Deprecation (RFC 9745) and Sunset (RFC 8594) headers added

facts.old: Pagination: cursor-based (opaque token) beats offset: stable under concurrent writes, O(1) on the DB, no page drift
facts.verdict: corrected: keyset is an index seek (logarithmic), measured flat 0.02 to 0.05 ms at every depth; offset measured linear to about 200 ms at 1M rows (Postgres 16.2, local)

facts.old: Offset survives only for small admin UIs
Return next_cursor (null when done), accept limit with a server cap, document the sort order
facts.where: Reading s-page rules; captured list exchange
facts.verdict: verified (AIP-158: empty next token is the only end signal; coerce or cap page size)

facts.old: Keyset pagination is the SQL implementation: WHERE (created, id) > (:c, :i) ORDER BY created, id
facts.verdict: verified (Postgres row comparison docs) and run

facts.old: Every mutating endpoint a client might retry (POST especially) accepts Idempotency-Key
facts.verdict: kept; Stripe: all POST requests accept keys

facts.old: Server atomically records key -> response and replays it for the retry window
facts.verdict: verified (Stripe docs: status and body saved, including 500s; 24 h); demo implements it

facts.old: Return a conflict if the same key arrives with a different payload
facts.verdict: corrected: IETF draft-07 says 422 for a different payload and 409 for a concurrent retry; Brandur's 2017 code used 409

facts.old: Idempotency keys make client retry policy safe; see Distributed Systems Basics
facts.where: Reading s-idem final note links Reliability engineering and Queues
facts.verdict: kept; link repointed to the new siblings

facts.old: Error taxonomy: HTTP status class (4xx yours, 5xx mine), stable string code, human message, param pointer, request_id
facts.where: Reading s-err (three layers, request ID, pointers)

facts.old: RFC 9457 (application/problem+json) is the standards-track shape
Distinguish retryable from non-retryable (429/503 + Retry-After vs 400)
Never leak internals in messages
Keep codes append-only (clients switch on them)
facts.verdict: kept; Anthropic: type values will grow over time

facts.old: OpenAI/Anthropic error shapes are the de-facto reference for LLM APIs
facts.where: Reading s-err (Anthropic shape verbatim from docs; OpenAI fields)
facts.verdict: Anthropic verified 2026-10-04; OpenAI field list marked unconfirmed on the page (x-request-id verified)

facts.old: Webhooks: the inverse API, inverse discipline
Sign payloads (HMAC with timestamp to stop replays)
facts.verdict: verified (Standard Webhooks; Stripe-Signature t=,v1=; 5-minute default tolerance)

facts.old: Deliver at-least-once so consumers must dedupe on event ID
facts.verdict: verified (Stripe: track event IDs; Standard Webhooks: webhook-id as idempotency key)

facts.old: Retry with backoff to a dead-letter state
facts.verdict: verified (Stripe up to three days; Standard Webhooks schedule)

facts.old: Order is not guaranteed (ship a sequence number or let consumers re-fetch current state)
Send thin events (IDs + type) when staleness or PII is a concern
facts.verdict: verified (Stripe offers thin and snapshot events)

facts.old: Provide a redelivery UI; every serious consumer asks for one
facts.where: Reading s-hook ('let the user redeliver'); Stripe manual resend 15/30 days not repeated

facts.old: Webhook details in Topic: protocols
facts.where: Reading s-sse note and Further reading link Topic: protocols

facts.old: Library and package design in Python: typed interfaces, mypy --strict, py.typed, Sequence/Mapping, Protocol, overload, NewType/Literal
Pydantic contracts at boundaries; parse, don't validate; pydantic-settings; dataclasses inside the core; pydantic earns its cost at IO boundaries
facts.where: Boundary half: Reading s-val (parse, don't validate; models at the edge, not deep inside). Library half: owned by code_design
facts.verdict: split: API side carried here, library side handed off

facts.old: Design the API surface small: __all__, one entry point, keyword-only args, no boolean positional flags, deep modules
Errors as a hierarchy: one base exception, subclasses per category, retryability in the type
Mechanics: pyproject + uv, semver, DeprecationWarning one minor before removal, Hyrum's law
facts.where: Hyrum's law: Reading s-what (verified quote, hyrumslaw.com) and Breaking or not? item 13. The rest owned by code_design

facts.old: Code review taste: Google standard, priority order, nit:, small PRs, ML review habits, LLM-authored code
facts.verdict: handed off; '90% of defects in the first few hundred lines' flagged unconfirmed for that builder

facts.old: When abstraction earns its keep: loan metaphor, rule of three, Sandi Metz, declarative config, plugin architectures, premature platformisation, cheap reversibility

added_beyond_old_page: HTTP byte by byte (RFC 9110, 9112, 9113), methods table with safe/idempotent, status code table, JSON pitfalls (RFC 8259, 3339), FastAPI service walk, validation captures, REST conventions (Fielding, AIP-121/136, RFC 7396, 5789), problem details members, request IDs, filtering rules, the IETF Idempotency-Key draft status and implementers, Brandur's atomic phases and recovery points, authentication and authorisation (RFC 6750, 6749, 7636, 9700, OAuth 2.1 draft-16, OIDC, RFC 7519, 8725, OWASP API1:2023), rate limit headers (RFC 6585, IETF RateLimit draft-11, OpenAI x-ratelimit headers), SSE (WHATWG) with production pitfalls, OpenAPI 3.1 and 3.2.0, gRPC vs REST, production checklist, common mistakes; real captures from a FastAPI 0.142.2 service and a Postgres 16.2 measurement.
